newsitem.title: UK: LME zinc off lows during choppy AM trading.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc off lows during choppy AM trading.

text.p: A volatile zinc market held traders attention during London Metal Exchange (LME) trading on Tuesday morning and several are expecting further fireworks in later trading.
Elsewhere, copper bounced from its lows, though traders remained wary to downside losses, while nickel moved higher on short-covering.
Referring to the zinc market one LME floor trader said, "We are not out of the woods yet as market positions are in disarray after the earlier plunge."

Earlier zinc prices dived to a low of $1,370 as general liquidation rocked an over extended market. Investment funds led the rout which took prices down from around seven-year highs on Monday when three months zinc peaked at $1,674.
Final morning business was at $1,480, well down on Monday's LME kerb close of $1,671.

Traders said talk circulated that a deal had been struck between Chinese short position holders and a European merchant, while several others suggested that the Chinese smelters were near square after buying forward late on Monday and earlier on Tuesday.
This helped to rock a market that was already looking for a downside correction given that its 14 day RSI had risen above 90 percent on the back of the recent strong rally.
However, one trader was quick to point out that nearby backwardations remained in place, "If a deal had been struck then you would expect the backwardations to disappear very quickly," he said.
Cash to three months was indicated at $75/$90 after approaching $100 on Monday.
Another factor that helped to unsettle the market was a small decline in LME stocks. The fall of 825 tonnes could signal an end to the recent string of sizeable drawdowns, traders said.
"The pace of declines looks to be slowing after weeks of talk of robust fundamenatals," one said.

Another stocks rise in copper prompted speculative selling to move prices to a low of $2,312, though short-covering and bargain hunting helped to lift the martket back to $2,345, a loss of $8 from Monday.
But with stocks rising in the slow summer period traders expect further downside pressure to emerge. "I would not be surprised if we see $2,300 by the end of the week," one floor trader said.

Nickel bounced on short-covering and trade buying to settle at $7,350, up $60. Traders said they expected a period of consolidation in nickel but warned any substantial losses in copper could turn the market.
Trading in aluminium was relatively calm. It was last at $1,677, up $3, while lead settled at $628, down $11.
